faqs.question: What is Electronics Engineering course?
faqs.answer: Electronics Engineering course is designed in order to prepare candidates for developing electronic equipments which are applied across various domains such as heavy machinery, saellite communication, radio communication etc. Electronics Engineering is either offered as a stand-alone course or it is offered as Electronics and Communications Engineering or Electrical and Electronics Engineering. This course is a branch of Electrical Engineering that requires candidates to develop skills in order to develop products and electronic systems using electronic technologies such as VLSI , Sonar , Radar, etc. With a duration of four years for BTech programs and three years for Diploma courses , Electronics Engineering equips graduates with competitive salary potential, particularly with experience and specialised skills. Moreover, it serves as a pathway to higher studies , facilitating pursuits in Master's programs like MTech in Electronics Engineering, Computer Science, or related fields , both nationally and internationally. Know more about - Electronics Engineering

faqs.question: What is the Electronics Engineering course duration?
faqs.answer: Electronics Engineering course duration generally differs depending on its level. For UG Electronics Engineering courses, its 4 years in general. If you are interested in courses at the PG level, the duration is 2 years. You can also go for a diploma in Electronics Engg. right after completing your Class 10, which is 3 years long , if you wish to enter the workforce at the earliest. Meanwhile, a PhD level course in Electronics Engineering can last between 3 years and 5 years , depending on your research topic and the college offering the program.

faqs.question: What is the BTech Electronics Engineering course fees in IITs and NITs?
faqs.answer: The Electronics Engineering course fees for BTech in the IITs and NITs are a bit expensive because of the reputation, ranking, and student popularity that they enjoy. Talking about the IITs, the BTech Electronics Engineering course fees is around INR 8 lakh, and for the NITs, the fees is approximately INR 5 lakh, which is subject to change as per new academic sessions every year. Know more about - Electronics Engineering

faqs.question: Do Electronics Engineering jobs require coding knowledge?
faqs.answer: You should surely have good knowledge of coding and programming for Electronics Engineering jobs that are about the design, testing and effective working of electronic devices and embedded systems. Not every job role requires extensive coding but tasks like circuit simulation, data analysis, automation, embedded systems design and IoT development need you to have a solid coding foundation. faqs.question: Is the BTech Electronics Engineering syllabus same across all colleges?
faqs.answer: The Electronics Engineering syllabus for the BTech degree is not the same across all colleges. Every college prefers to follow an individual coursework module that includes both theory classes and practical lab work. While core subjects and fundamental concepts might be similar, the structure, electives offered, and laboratory and project work are different. You can check the detailed syllabus for the course on the respective college websites that you're targeting to get a clearer picture.

faqs.question: Which Electronics Engineering subjects are taught in the first year of BTech?
faqs.answer: The Electronics Engineering subjects for the BTech course vary from college to college but some core subjects taught in the first year are usually the same. The first year is usually seen as the foundational year where you're taught about the basics to set the base for more electronic field-specific and advanced subject modules. Some important subjects in the Electronics Engineering syllabus for 1 st year BTech course are given below: Engineering Mathematics Engineering Physics Engineering Chemistry Computer Programming Differential Equations Fundamentals of Electronics & Electrical Engineering Linear Algebra & Complex Analysis Engineering Graphics

faqs.question: Does the BTech Electronics Engineering syllabus focus more on theory or practical application?
faqs.answer: It covers both. The syllabus for B Tech in Electronics Engineering covers both via lab work and industrial projects . Both the theory classes and practical labs are important for students to understand the nuances of the field and become job-ready for the future. Top recruiters in the business world also look for technical proficiency, practical knowledge, and theoretical understanding in the candidates who can excel at work and drive profitability.

faqs.question: What is the selection criteria for BTech Electronics Engineering course?

blocks.value: The selection criteria for admission to the B Tech Electronics Engineering course involves both entrance exam scores and Class 12 board exam marks . A majority of the top-ranked colleges prefer valid entrance exam scores like JEE Main, JEE Advanced, Andhra Pradesh EAMCET, MHT CET, etc.

Having said that, there are more than 450 BTech Electronics engineering colleges that give admission on the basis of Class 12 merit and often end up taking extra rounds like the GD or PI to test the capability of the students.

faqs.question: How to secure admission to Electronics Engineering courses at the IITs in India?

blocks.value: For taking admission to Electronics Engineering courses at the IITs, you should be able to meet the eligibility requirements. For UG courses, you should have at least 75% marks in Class 12 in the PCM subjects . If you belong to the reserved category, the marks eligibility requirement is usually relaxed to a certain extent. Also, you have to appear for the JEE Main and JEE Advanced exams. You should work very hard and get a good rank in JEE Main to be eligible for JEE Advanced, which serves as the final call for admission.

After you successfully secure a decent rank in JEE Advanced, you will have to appear for the JOSAA counselling process where you will be allotted a seat according to your rank at one of the IIT branches in India. Similarly, for PG courses in Electronics Engg., you should meet the eligibility criteria of 60% marks in your bachelor's degree in the same or related field and clear the GATE exam . The good news is, if you are an IIT graduate with a CGPA of 8 or above, you need not give the exam and are eligible for direct admission to the M.Tech course at a few IITs.

career.title: Electronics Engineering Career Guide: Roles, Salary & Future Scope
intro: The Electronics Engineering career in India has a booming market because of the technological advancements taking place every day, empowering the world by moving towards automation and robotics in almost all of the work fields. The society today is looking for innovation, experimentation, convenience, and the best internet connectivity, which hints at the promising Electronics Engineering scope in India .

Electronics Engineering professionals are involved in the designing, planning, building and testing of electronic systems and devices. Some of the popular fresher jobs in India include VLSI Design Engineer, Embedded Systems Engineer, Electronics and Communication Engineer, Network Planning Engineer , IoT Engineer, etc.

There are so many Electronics Engineering career opportunities in different work sectors like consumer electronics, telecommunications, IT and software, manufacturing, healthcare, aerospace, etc. The average salary in India is between INR 4 LPA and INR 8 LPA. Top recruiters in this field include Intel, Nvidia, Texas Instruments, Qualcomm, Infosys, Samsung Electronics, Wipro, Dell, Bosch India, Sony, etc.
Interested students may continue reading the article to know everything about the Electronics Engineering careers for freshers .

answers.answer_text: With 86.9 percentile in MHT-CET and aiming for CSE, you can get admission in good private colleges but not top government ones.
